audit.finding: F-VQ17 qualifies composition through the existing shared SWAP kernel/runtime path; no use-case-specific kernel is introduced.
No kernel I/O or legacy file parsing is introduced; F-VQ17 adds qualification-only tests, runner, workflow and evidence.
The exercised runtime keeps parameters, forcing, committed state, numerical configuration, results and diagnostics explicitly separated.
SNOW continuation state is allocated only for active SNOW columns; inactive columns retain no SNOW persistent state.
Solver and algebraic workspaces remain execution-local; F-VQ17 introduces no persistent per-column scratch.

Qualification covers deterministic batching and canonical aggregation without adding a second aggregate sort, but it does not qualify 100k-column scaling or the pre-existing execution-order insertion sort.
Checkpoint, trial, rollback, replay and commit are executed; rejected trials leave committed state unchanged and replay is bitwise exact.
A/B/A and checkpoint replay are exact for the admitted scope; no hidden physical warm-start state is introduced.
A non-midnight exact one-day interval is admitted. Subdaily and multiday SNOW paths fail closed; arbitrary-duration SNOW physics remains unqualified.
No coupling-window duration is hard-coded by F-VQ17; the one-day restriction belongs only to the currently qualified SNOW process event semantics.
Coupling transaction semantics are not modified and remain compatible with rollback/retry requirements.
The groundwater head/flux interface contract is not changed by this qualification.
Per-column and authoritative aggregate mass are complete with zero missing-contribution mask; melt is retained as an internal transfer and no tolerance is relaxed.
No groundwater response tangent is introduced or modified.
No extra production coupling runs or finite-difference tangent policy is introduced.

Real-physics MultiSWAP is independently verified for 1, 2, 17 and 31 columns and multiple batch partitions, but performance at 100k columns and real-physics parallelism are explicitly outside admission.
No 1:1 SWAP-to-MODFLOW mapping assumption is introduced.
Deep-vadose transfer-zone behavior is not part of F-VQ17.
No deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition is modified.
Architecture remains open to alternative soil-water solvers; scientific admission here is deliberately restricted to the exercised equilibrium Richards profile.
The qualified F-VQ16 B1.10 SNOW process is reused through the runtime composition; no duplicate SNOW physics path is introduced.
SNOW qualification uses the public process/runtime seams and does not couple process code to HeadCalc internals.
Physics configuration and numerical execution policy remain separate; F-VQ17 admits no balanced, throughput or fallback physics modification.
No bounded-cost fallback is admitted. Predictable-cost/performance qualification remains F-PE owned.
Reference accuracy remains available; the exact F-VQ16/B1.10 SNOW oracle is replayed and no reduced-accuracy substitute is admitted.
Per-column completion, solver execution, commit provenance, aggregate mass, serialization and failure diagnostics are exercised and persisted in qualification evidence.
All-inactive cases verify zero SNOW optional state; SNOW state is paid only by active columns.
Tile fractions, transfer zones and MODFLOW system composition remain outside the SWAP kernel/runtime candidate assessed here.
The admitted run starts at non-midnight t0=2300.375 and depends on no .swp path or MODFLOW presence; the one-day SNOW restriction is explicit rather than hidden.
All architecture invariants are explicitly reassessed for the F-MR06 SNOW MultiSWAP scientific admission.

qualified_holds: Subdaily, multiday and arbitrary-duration SNOW remain unqualified.
General non-equilibrium Richards behavior remains unqualified by F-VQ17.
100k-column performance and asymptotic scaling remain unqualified.
Balanced, throughput and fallback execution policies remain F-PE owned and unqualified here.
Final MultiSWAP production admission remains F-MQ24 owned.
